Steps.1: Review the schematic design of the hw_DAA. Check that the Ethernet has an oscillator of 25MHz.
Steps.2: Connect the hw_DAA to a DAA CS harness.
Steps.3: Connect the power supply to the DAA CS harness power input, using a DC power connector, banana cables, and crocodile clips (according to the attached diagram).
Steps.4: Switch on the power supply source.
Steps.5: Set 12V and 3A on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.6: Turn on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.8: Connect on CH1 an oscilloscope probe to OUT signal (pin 3 of the Y4) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.9: Set the vertical grid to 500 mV/div.
Steps.10: Set the horizontal grid to ~100 ns/div and center the horizontal trigger position around the center of the oscilloscope screen.
Steps.11: Ensure that the attenuation is set to x10 and BW limit to 200 MHz (CH1).
Steps.12: Set the trigger level to ~1V, rising edge and source the CH1.
Steps.13: Click on the Stop/Run button to capture the output of the oscillator.
Steps.14: Using the horizontal menu of the measure tab, click on frequency (Freq).
Steps.18: Set up the multimeter as voltmeter. Ensure it is set to Auto-Range, Run/Hold and DC Voltage.
Steps.19: Connect the positive lead of the multimeter to the VCC pin of the Ethernet Oscillator (pin 4 of the Y4 or at C320 pad) and the negative lead to GND.
Steps.20: Measure with the multimeter and check if it is supplied by 1.8V.
